title: The Classroom Temperature Debate
passage:
In early summer, Class 2A argued almost every day about the air conditioner. Students near the windows felt hot in the afternoon sun, while students directly below the air vents complained that they were cold. Someone changed the temperature setting whenever the teacher looked away. By the end of the week, the remote control had become an object of conflict.

The teacher could have set one fixed temperature and forbidden changes. Instead, she asked the class to collect evidence. For three days, students placed simple thermometers at six locations and recorded temperatures every hour. They also marked whether sunlight was reaching each area and asked students to rate how comfortable they felt.

The results showed that one thermostat setting did not create one classroom temperature. At two in the afternoon, the sunny window area could be almost four degrees warmer than the desks near the strongest vent. Comfort ratings also differed even at similar temperatures. Some students preferred cooler air, while others felt cold easily.

The class first tried lowering blinds on the sunny windows. This reduced the temperature difference but also made the room darker. They adjusted only the upper parts of the blinds so natural light could still enter. They then redirected two vent covers slightly upward to reduce direct cold air on students. These small physical changes made the room more even before anyone touched the thermostat.

Next, the class agreed on a temperature range rather than one exact setting. If most readings stayed within the range, the remote would not be changed immediately because one person's discomfort might be caused by location rather than the whole room. Students who still felt cold could keep a light sweater at school, while seating near the hottest windows rotated every two weeks.

The discussion did not eliminate every complaint. On humid days, the same temperature felt warmer, and after physical education some students wanted stronger cooling. The class added a short ventilation period after lunch and accepted that temporary adjustments were sometimes reasonable. The rules became guidelines rather than rigid commands.

By July, arguments about the remote had nearly disappeared. The class had not discovered a perfect temperature. Instead, they had learned that the original debate had been framed too simply. ‘What temperature should the air conditioner be?’ assumed that everyone experienced the same environment. In reality, sunlight, airflow, humidity, clothing, activity, and individual preference all mattered. Once the class addressed the differences in the room, the number on the thermostat became less important. The students learned that disagreements sometimes persist not because people refuse to compromise, but because they are responding honestly to different conditions.
translation:
初夏、2Aではエアコン温度をめぐる口論が毎日のように起きていました。窓側は午後の日差しで暑く、吹き出し口の真下は寒く、先生が見ていない間に誰かが設定温度を変えていました。

先生は一つの温度を固定する代わりに、証拠を集めようと提案しました。六か所に温度計を置き、三日間、一時間ごとの温度、日差しの有無、各自の快適さを記録しました。

結果、同じ設定でも教室内の温度は同じではないと分かりました。午後二時には日なたの窓側が強い吹き出し口付近より四度近く高いことがあり、同じ温度でも暑いと感じる人、寒いと感じる人がいました。

まず日当たりの強い窓のブラインドを下げました。温度差は減りましたが暗くなったため、上側だけ調整して自然光を残しました。さらに二つの吹き出し口を少し上向きにし、直接冷風が当たりにくくしました。設定温度を変える前に物理的な差を小さくしたのです。

次に一つの数字ではなく温度範囲を決めました。多くの場所が範囲内なら、誰か一人が不快でもすぐ設定を変えず、場所の影響を考えます。寒がりの生徒は薄手の上着を置き、暑い窓側の席は二週間ごとに交代しました。

湿度が高い日や体育後など、同じ温度でも状況が違うため、昼休み後に短時間換気し、必要なら一時調整することも認めました。規則は絶対命令ではなく目安になりました。

七月にはリモコンをめぐる争いはほぼなくなりました。完璧な温度を発見したのではありません。『エアコンを何度にするか』という最初の問いが単純すぎたのです。日差し、風、湿度、服装、活動量、個人差があり、人は本当に異なる条件へ反応していました。教室内の差を減らすと、設定数字そのものの重要性が下がりました。対立が続くのは妥協する気がないからではなく、異なる現実を経験しているからという場合もあるのです。
